instruction: Implement the bubble sort algorithm in 'bubbleSort.py' on the Desktop by referencing 'Bubble_Sort_tutorial.docx'. Execute the program and redirect its output to 'res.txt' on the Desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires implementing bubble sort, running code, and saving output to res.txt. Evaluator checks that output contains keywords 'Sorted' and 'array' (50% weight) and all 7 sorted numbers [11, 12, 22, 25, 34, 64, 90] (50% weight). Provides partial credit for partial completion.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for keywords, 0.5 for all numbers present

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts text content from res.txt as list of lines, handling file existence and encoding errors
Metric logic correctly checks for keywords case-insensitively (50% weight) and extracts/validates all 7 sorted numbers (50% weight)
Expected values are semantically correct - keywords 'Sorted' and 'array' indicate sorting output, numbers [11, 12, 22, 25, 34, 64, 90] represent sorted result
Partial credit logic is appropriate with 50/50 weighting between keywords and numbers
Evaluator successfully verifies the END RESULT (correct output in res.txt exists with expected content)
No postconfig needed - output file persists after program execution
Regex number extraction (\d+) is robust and will work with various output formats
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor coverage gap: Evaluator only verifies final output exists with correct content, but does not verify intermediate steps (bubbleSort.py was modified, program was executed). However, this is acceptable for outcome-based evaluation.
Consider: Evaluator is lenient and checks only for presence of keywords/numbers, not exact output format. This is reasonable for educational tasks but may accept outputs with extra content.
